hints: Plot cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries: $(20, 32), (30, 66), (35, 112), (40, 178), (50, 228), (60, 250)$.
Anchor the graph at the origin $(0, 0)$.
Join the points with a smooth increasing curve or continuous line segments.
walkthrough:
Identify the upper class boundaries and their corresponding cumulative frequencies:
$$(0, 0), (20, 32), (30, 66), (35, 112), (40, 178), (50, 228), (60, 250)$$
Set up linear axes: horizontal axis for time $t$ from $0$ to $60$ minutes, and vertical axis for cumulative frequency from $0$ to $250$.
Plot each point precisely at the upper boundary of its class interval.
Draw a smooth increasing cumulative frequency curve (or connected line segments) starting from $(0, 0)$ and ending at $(60, 250)$.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the coordinates to plot.
In a cumulative frequency graph, frequencies must always be plotted at the upper class boundary of each interval:
- $t \le 0$: cumulative frequency $= 0 \implies (0, 0)$
- $t \le 20$: cumulative frequency $= 32 \implies (20, 32)$
- $t \le 30$: cumulative frequency $= 66 \implies (30, 66)$
- $t \le 35$: cumulative frequency $= 112 \implies (35, 112)$
- $t \le 40$: cumulative frequency $= 178 \implies (40, 178)$
- $t \le 50$: cumulative frequency $= 228 \implies (50, 228)$
- $t \le 60$: cumulative frequency $= 250 \implies (60, 250)$

Step 2: Plot axes and curve.
- Horizontal axis: Time $t$ (minutes), scaled linearly $0$ to $60$.
- Vertical axis: Cumulative frequency, scaled linearly $0$ to $250$.
- Connect the points with an increasing curve or ogive anchored at $(0, 0)$.

ai_rubric.Constructing Cumulative Frequency Graphs: Plots points at upper boundaries (20,32), (30,66), (35,112), (40,178), (50,228), (60,250) and joins to (0,0). For this part: Draw a cumulative frequency graph to illustrate the data.

hints: Find the cumulative frequency corresponding to the 60th percentile: $0.60 \times 250 = 150$.
Locate 150 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and move horizontally to intersect your curve.
Read the corresponding time $t$ on the horizontal axis (acceptable range 37 to 39 minutes).
walkthrough:
Calculate the rank of the 60th percentile for $N = 250$ members:
$$\text{Position} = 0.60 \times 250 = 150$$
Locate $150$ on the vertical axis of the cumulative frequency graph.

Read horizontally across to the curve and vertically down to the horizontal time axis:
$$t \approx 38\text{ minutes}$$
State the estimate, noting that values in the interval $37 \le t \le 39$ are accepted.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Calculate the cumulative frequency value.
To find the 60th percentile, compute $60\%$ of the total frequency $N = 250$:
$$0.60 \times 250 = 150$$

Step 2: Read from the graph.
- Draw a horizontal line from $150$ on the vertical cumulative frequency axis until it meets the curve.
- From that intersection point, drop a vertical line to the horizontal axis.
- The reading on the time axis is approximately $38$ minutes.
Any value in the range $37 \le t \le 39$ minutes is accepted based on the graph.

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative Frequency Graphs: Finds 60% of 250 = 150 and reads approx 38 minutes (accept 37 <= t <= 39). For this part: Use your graph to estimate the 60th percentile of the data.

skill_tags: Estimating Standard Deviation from Grouped Data

hints: Determine the individual class frequencies by taking successive differences of the cumulative frequencies: 32, 34, 46, 66, 50, 22.
Compute $\sum fm^2 = 333\,650$ and use the given mean $\bar{t} = 34.4$ to calculate the variance and standard deviation.
walkthrough:
Compute the variance using the given mean $\bar{t} = 34.4$:
$$s^2 = \frac{\sum fm^2}{N} - \bar{t}^2 = \frac{333\,650}{250} - (34.4)^2 = 1334.6 - 1183.36 = 151.24$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Reconstruct class frequencies and identify midpoints.
From the cumulative frequencies:
- Interval $[0, 20)$: $f = 32$, midpoint $m = 10$
- Interval $[20, 30)$: $f = 66 - 32 = 34$, midpoint $m = 25$
- Interval $[30, 35)$: $f = 112 - 66 = 46$, midpoint $m = 32.5$
- Interval $[35, 40)$: $f = 178 - 112 = 66$, midpoint $m = 37.5$
- Interval $[40, 50)$: $f = 228 - 178 = 50$, midpoint $m = 45$
- Interval $[50, 60)$: $f = 250 - 228 = 22$, midpoint $m = 55$
Total frequency $\sum f = 250$.

Step 2: Calculate $\sum fm^2$.
- $32 \times 10^2 = 3200$
- $34 \times 25^2 = 34 \times 625 = 21\,250$
- $46 \times 32.5^2 = 46 \times 1056.25 = 48\,587.5$
- $66 \times 37.5^2 = 66 \times 1406.25 = 92\,812.5$
- $50 \times 45^2 = 50 \times 2025 = 101\,250$
- $22 \times 55^2 = 22 \times 3025 = 66\,550$
Sum:
$$\sum fm^2 = 3200 + 21\,250 + 48\,587.5 + 92\,812.5 + 101\,250 + 66\,550 = 333\,650$$

Step 3: Calculate the variance.
Using the given mean $\bar{t} = 34.4$:
$$\text{Variance} = \frac{\sum fm^2}{\sum f} - \bar{t}^2$$
$$\text{Variance} = \frac{333\,650}{250} - 34.4^2 = 1334.6 - 1183.36 = 151.24$$

Step 4: Take the square root.
$$s = \sqrt{151.24} \approx 12.2979...$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $12.3$ minutes.

ai_rubric.Estimating Standard Deviation from Group: Computes sum(fm^2) = 333650, variance = 151.24, and standard deviation = 12.3 minutes. For this part: Calculate an estimate for the standard deviation of the times taken to complete the challenge by these 250 members.
